extracted.intended_audience: new NIH grant applicants (new grantees) and NIH peer reviewers / SROs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on NIH grant application assignment, reviewer conduct, conflicts, confidentiality, review meeting procedures, scoring (including the Simplified Review Framework effective Jan 25, 2025), and resubmission rules. Aimed at helping applicants and reviewers understand processes and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to Institutes or Centers (ICs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to Institutes or Centers based on the overall mission and guidelines of the IC and the specific programmatic mandates and interests of the IC. Applications can only be assigned to ICs participating in the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help your application get to the right institute by copying the abstract/Aims into tools like Matchmaker; Matchmaker returns a list of Institutes, funded grants, and links to Program Officials. Use the Assignment Request Form to make assignment suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to Scientific Review Groups (Study Sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assigned to scientific review groups (CSR study sections) based on specific, published review guidelines for each review group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions made in the Assignment Request Form (ARF) are considered. Within a Review Branch, assignment can be to standing study sections when subject matter matches referral guidelines, or to Special Emphasis Panels (SEPs) when subject matter doesn't fit, for one-time conflicts/initiatives, or when assignment would create a conflict. Use keyword search, the Assisted Referral Tool (ART), and CSR study section descriptions to identify appropriate study sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Request Form (ARF) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARF replaces many functions of the cover letter and should be used to make assignment suggestions (study section and institute), list areas of expertise needed to evaluate the application, and identify potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suggest specific reviewers on the ARF. Use it to help ensure the application reaches an appropriate IC and study section and to indicate expertise needed for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Conflicts of Interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a reviewer COI: institutional conflicts; family member/close friend; collaborator/Key Personnel; longstanding scientific disagreement; personal bias; appearance of conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow NIH COI policies (link provided). Any member in conflict with an application must leave the room during discussion. Applicants should identify potential conflicts on ARF; reviewers and staff should consult COI guidance at grants.nih.gov/ grants/ peer/ peer_coi.htm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Review materials and proceedings of review meetings are confidential information for reviewers and NIH staff. At the end of each meeting, reviewers must destroy or return all review-related material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not discuss review proceedings with anyone except the Scientific Review Officer (SRO); questions concerning review proceedings should be referred to the SRO. Applicants should never communicate directly with study section members about an application. The statute of confidentiality is life-long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review integrity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and contacts for reporting concerns or questions about possible violations of peer review integrity, respectful interactions, bias, or anything affecting fairness of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your SRO, CSR Review Integrity Officer (csrrio@mail.nih.gov), NIH Review Policy Officer (reviewpolicyofficer@mail.nih.gov), or send messages to reportbias@csr.nih.gov for issues related to bias or fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting reviewer assignments and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application is assigned to three or more reviewers 5-6 weeks in advance. Reviewers assess each application by providing a preliminary Overall Impact score, criterion scores, a comment on appropriateness of the budget, and a written critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should prepare these elements ahead of the meeting; the preliminary scores and critiques form the basis for discussion and final scoring at the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Review Framework — goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals of the Simplified Framework: enable reviewers to better focus on key questions necessary to assess scientific and technical merit (e.g., should and can the proposed research be conducted), mitigate reputational bias, and reduce reviewer burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to most research project applications submitted for January 25, 2025 due dates and after; check the Guide Notice NOT-OD-24-010 and NIH resources for details, guidance for reviewers and applicants, training, FAQs, and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Simplified Framework)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor asks whether the research addresses important problems/opportunities and whether it advances or innovates in the field; it is scored numerically and contributes to the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Simplified Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers on Approach (and includes inclusions and study timeline for clinical trials). Scored 1-9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates methodological rigor, feasibility of the proposed approach, and, for clinical trials, inclusions and study timelines. Scored numerically and contributes to overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Simplified Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and Environment are evaluated as appropriate or gaps identified; these are considered in the overall impact but do not receive individual numeric scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gaps are identified in investigators or environment, they require explanation. This change is intended to reduce reputational bias by not assigning separate numeric scores to investigator/environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous five scored criteria (pre-Simplified Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before Jan 25, 2025 the five review criteria were Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, and Environment — each scored individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the old system each criterion received a numeric score; the Simplified Framework reorganizes these into three factors with changed scoring and treatment of Investigator/Environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application discussion and meeting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: At the meeting, any member in conflict leaves the room. Reviewer 1 introduces and presents the critique; Reviewers 2 and 3 highlight new issues and areas that significantly impact scores. All members without a conflict are invited to join the discussion and then vote on the final Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About half of applications will be discussed; applications unanimously judged by the committee to be in the lower half are not discussed. Applications to be discussed are reviewed in random order within each cluster. New Investigator R01s and some application types may be clustered together for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact is defined as the likelihood for a project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. Evaluate Overall Impact by considering the five criteria (significance, investigator, innovation, approach, environment) weighted by the reviewer's judgment and other score influences (e.g., human subjects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores are on the NIH 1-9 scale; the guidance notes that a score of 5 represents a good medium-impact application. Consideration of criteria and other influences should inform the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH resubmission policy and timing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: After an unsuccessful new (A0) or unsuccessful resubmission (A1), you may submit a new (A0) application with the same idea only after your summary statement has been issued. NIH will not accept an A0 or A1 that overlaps a funded application, simultaneous submissions of overlapping applications, or an A0 or A1 submitted before NIH issues the summary statement of an earlier, overlapping application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must wait for the summary statement and avoid overlap with funded or simultaneously submitted applications. See resubmission FAQs for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: New application must be written as new (no referencing prior review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new (A0) application should not contain information that might bias the review or provide a competitive advantage. You cannot refer to a previous review (no mention of previous score or reviewer comments or how the A0 is responsive) and you cannot submit elements of a renewal (no progress report or progress report publication list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mark text to indicate changes or reference prior critiques; write the application as a standalone, new submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer sourcing and recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources for finding reviewers include successful applicants, recommendations from reviewers and NIH staff, NIH RePORTER (Project Reporter), NIH PI and reviewer databases, the Internet, and scientific conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff and SROs use these sources to identify potential reviewers; applicants should not suggest specific reviewers but can identify needed expertise on the ARF.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH peer review resources and where to learn more
rubrics_metrics.description: List of NIH and CSR web resources for policies, guidance, electronic submission, CSR study section descriptions, rosters, meeting dates, and resources for applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant links include NIH main site, Office of Extramural Research, Grants Policy, Electronic Submission/OER/ERA pages, CSR resources for applicants, CSR Study Section Descriptions, and CSR rosters and meeting dates.
